result.title: No Corners Cut: State-Grounded Transitions for Mid-Stream Prompt Switches in Video Generation
result.summary: Streaming video generators allow users to dynamically modulate video synthesis via mid-stream prompt switching. Existing streaming methods can respond to the updated instruction while still cutting corners, prematurely realizing goals or taking heuristic shortcuts that bypass necessary intermediate state changes needed for a plausible transition. In this study, we present SEGUE, a novel framework that makes this process explicit and trains the generator to execute these transitions faithfully. At each switch, a training-free planner parses the latest frame and prompts, writes a few segue prompts with roles and durations, and then hands control back to the user's prompt. Furthermore, to address the inherent difficulty of training causal models on short-lived temporal schedules without corrupting preparatory supervision, we introduce SPANDMD, which evaluates each active prompt using the full rollout as temporal context while retaining its DMD residual only within the prompt's assigned span. On OpenTrans-360, a benchmark of 1,800 switches that scores how the old state exits and the new one begins, SEGUE ranks first on all eight transition metrics and raises the overall score over the strongest baseline from 0.866 to 0.887. It also ranks first on four of six instruction-response metrics of StreamAV-Bench, while the planner transfers to frozen autoregressive generators without retraining.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SEGUE 框架，针对流式视频生成中「中途切换提示词」场景，用免训练规划器生成带角色与时长的过渡提示，并设计 SPANDMD 训练目标，让生成器忠实执行旧状态退出与新状态进入的中间状态变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按时间跨度分配监督、避免短时调度污染准备性监督」的思路，可能为 LVR 中轨迹训练与贡献分配、以及 THINK/LOOK/STOP 等状态切换时机的监督提供概念类比，但研究对象是视频生成而非多模态推理，需较多核查。
